## How to Deposit

Deposits are submitted through GitHub. This ensures full version control, transparent review, public audit trail, and zero platform lock-in.

1. Submit

Open an issue on the Alexanarch repository using the deposit template. Attach your file and fill in the metadata fields.

2. Mint

Minting is automatic. An AXN identifier is computed from the content hash. The deposit is added to the registry. The record page goes live. The identifier is permanent. No prior review gates minting; the registry records what is submitted.

3. Review (if contested)

If a deposit is contested — on grounds of authorship, provenance, scope, or accuracy — the commitment is to read the content, not to pattern-match its substrate or its surface markers. The Obelus Principle governs the contested case: judgment follows from reading. Review applies in contestation; it is not a precondition for minting.

Deposit a Work Browse the Collection

## Infrastructure Properties

Properties of persistent scholarly infrastructure. Each is verifiable from the surfaces below and from the public protocol catalog at `/api/index.json`.

  * Content-derived identifiers — AXN: 6-emoji derivation from the first 6 bytes of SHA-256 of canonical bytes. The address is computed from the work; no host issues it.
  * Sovereign custody — mirrored across alexanarch.org, GitHub, content-addressable manifests (`SHA256SUMS.txt`), and machine-readable chunks (`/data/chunks/registry/`). Reconstruction verifiable from any complete mirror.
  * Tombstone permanence — withdrawn records retain bibliographic metadata, withdrawal reason, provenance chain, and canonical content hash. No record ever resolves to 410.
  * Public, machine-readable validation — every protocol at `/api/deposit-protocol.json`, `/api/axn-protocol.json`; central catalog at `/api/index.json`. No private moderation surface.
  * Substrate as standard metadata — methodology and substrate are declared fields in the registry schema. Provenance, not suspicion.
  * Falsification conditions as standard field — the work declares what would weaken or invalidate its claims. Part of the bibliographic record.
  * Legacy resolution — prior Zenodo DOIs preserved as resolvable aliases in the DOI Resolution Index; earlier AXN schema versions preserved in `legacy_axn` and `axn_history` fields.
  * Open licensing — CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC0-1.0. No license that constrains downstream reuse.
  * No cost. No account requirement to read. Anyone can read; anyone can verify; anyone can mirror.

How an audit gets built

  1. Start from the status The mark's Online Status printout from the TMO website is the one document the audit cannot be built without. Everything else is optional depth.
  2. Add what the file holds TMO records — the application as filed, examination reports, journal extracts, certificates, POAs, assignment deeds. The client mail chain. Prior-agent papers. Or skip the uploads entirely: a finished Talk to TMO fetch feeds the audit with one click.

### Note

Included only when genuinely warranted — enforcement risks, non-use vulnerability, third-party threats.

An audit is how a firm takes custody of a mark — the new client, the prior-agent handover, the portfolio acquired mid-prosecution, the pre-enforcement check. The question is always the same: what is this file, really? The Audit Report answers it in the format the firm already signs, from the documents the register already holds — and with Talk to TMO on the same platform, the whole loop closes: fetched from the Registry in the morning, audited before lunch.

Blank beats invented

Every fact in the report is extracted exclusively from the uploaded documents. A particular the papers don't state is left blank — never guessed. Where the documents are incomplete and a conclusion must be drawn, it is drawn in the open: “we are of the understanding that…”, in italics, labelled as inference.

Client correspondence is treated as instructions and context, never as verified fact: it supplies the client's reference, comments and questions, but it does not override the online record on status, dates or specification. Where the two conflict, the report flags the discrepancy for resolution instead of quietly choosing a side.

The trichotomy is illustrated below: first on the real line, then on the complex plane. On the real line, absolute convergence holds on the open interval \((-R, R)\), gross divergence outside, and the two boundary points \(\pm R\) are undecided. Image

In the complex plane, the absolute-convergence region is a full open disk of radius \(R\), the divergence region is its exterior, and the boundary circle \(C(0, R)\) is the «cercle d'incertitude». Image

Example — Three boundary regimes at \(R \equal 1\)

The three series \(\sum z^n\), \(\sum z^n/n^2\), \(\sum z^n/n\) all have radius \(R = 1\) (by d'Alembert below), yet their boundary behaviours differ:

  * \(\sum z^n\) at \(|z| = 1\): \(|z^n| = 1\) does not tend to \(0\), gross divergence everywhere on the unit circle;
  * \(\sum z^n/n^2\) at \(|z| = 1\): \(|z^n/n^2| = 1/n^2\) defines a Riemann-convergent numerical series, absolute convergence everywhere on the unit circle;
  * \(\sum z^n/n\) at \(z = 1\): harmonic series, divergence; at \(z = -1\): alternating-harmonic series, semi-convergence (converges by Leibniz, not absolutely). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
